thread:
amelia: opening escalation for ticket #78912 — customer in EU (tenant-acme-eu) reports sudden 401s + >1s p99 after enabling Dedicated capacity. They swear they pinned region=eu-west-1 but traces show hosted fallback and unexpected charges. Attaching snippets below.

sandeep: can you paste a request_id + sample curl? :eyes:

amelia: request_id=rid_0a9f3b2d. sample curl they used:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \\n  -H "x-redwood-tenant: tenant-acme-eu" \\n  -H "x-redwood-region: eu-west-1" \\n  -d '{"model":"gpt-small","prompt":"hi"}'
```
They set region header eu-west-1 but routing logs show route=hosted-eu-west-1 and fallback_reason=dedicated_capacity_full(us-east-1).

marie: pasting routing log excerpt:
```
[2026-03-10T14:12:34Z] rid=rid_0a9f3b2d route=dedicated-us-east-1 -> fallback hosted-eu-west-1 reason=decider:region_pin_mismatch
[2026-03-10T14:12:34Z] auth=200 token_owner=tenant-acme-eu
[2026-03-10T14:12:34Z] latency=1200ms bytes=18KB
```

ryan: quick hypothesis: autoscaler in us-east reported "full" due to stale heartbeat, global fallback policy then selected the nearest hosted pool (EU) which caused cross-region hop + cost. Also double-check if tenant got accidentally pinned to us-east in org config. :thinking:

amelia: customer insists they pinned to eu-west-1 in their org settings UI. They only see hosted-billing spike starting 14:12 UTC.

billing-bot: ALERT: tenant-acme-eu incurred 14,312 tokens on hosted pools between 2026-03-10T14:12 and 2026-03-10T14:20 — flagged for ops review. :warning:

infra-oncall: I can reproduce by simulating a node heartbeat drop for the dedicated-us-east-1 pool. Repro steps: 
1) rdrctl simulate-heartbeat --pool dedicated-us-east-1 --drop
2) run the curl above
3) inspect route with: 
```
rdrctl routes inspect rid_0a9f3b2d
```
Output shows pool_selector matched 'nearest' but region_pin=false, then fallback to hosted global.

sandeep: short-term mitigation: enable strict_region_pin=true for tenant or set header x-redwood-prefer-pool: dedicated to force no fallback. I can flip strict_region_pin on for tenant-acme-eu if ops approves.

ryan: long-term fix: change decider behavior so that if tenant has region pin set in org config, ignore autoscaler 'full' from other regions — i.e., prefer same-region hosted only when the pin is missing. Also shorten autoscaler heartbeat TTL and add more conservative capacity read. I'll open infra PR.

amelia: customer asking for ETA + refund. Also wondered if we can rollback recent autoscaler tweak (deploy 2026-03-09 22:05 UTC) that made fallback more aggressive.

infra-oncall: initiating rollback to previous autoscaler canary now. ETA ~15m. ops-bot kicked off deploy dpl-885.

marie: logging improvement TODO: include fields fallback_pool_type and capacity_report_version in route logs to make triage easier.

ops-bot: deploy dpl-885 started — status: in_progress

infra-oncall: rollback completed. Please retest.

ryan: validated with same curl after rollback — route now stays in eu-west-1, p50~85ms, no hosted fallback. Verified rid=rid_0a9f3b2d follow-up shows route=dedicated-eu-west-1.

amelia: customer confirmed recovery and reduced latency. They still require billing review for the hosted overflow charges.

billing-bot: Refund initiated for tenant-acme-eu for hosted overflow charges — reference BR-4321.

sandeep: postmortem action items: [1] tighten autoscaler heartbeat TTL and detection, [2] add tenant-level override to block-hosted-fallback (strict_region_pin), [3] surface autoscaler capacity metrics in console, [4] enrich route logs with fallback metadata.

amelia: thanks team. I'll close the escalation after billing confirms refund. :thumbsup:
